body.objective: Promote Smith normal form from a matrix primitive to a first-class integral and filtered complex layer. Rational cohomology misses torsion, discrete flux sectors and extension data that matter for compact gauge groups, bundle topology and global anomalies; Conflux must preserve those distinctions when comparing local and global reductions.
body.stop_condition: Provide finite free and finitely presented chain/cochain complexes over Z and declared PIDs; homology/cohomology decomposed into free and torsion invariant factors; constructive cycles, boundaries and torsion witnesses; universal-coefficient and long-exact-sequence maps with extension ledgers; cup products on supplied finite complexes; linking pairings and quadratic refinements for declared finite torsion groups; filtered complexes, exact persistence modules/barcodes and integral spectral-sequence pages to a declared bound. Demonstrate on a lens-space control, a compact U(1) charge matrix and one magnetic-bundle/global-anomaly fixture; show a pair of complexes that are rationally indistinguishable but integrally distinct, and export the distinguishing torsion/linking witness to Conflux.
body.forbid: no rational rank used to declare integral equivalence; no SNF diagonal accepted without unimodular transformation witnesses or independent verification; no torsion class discarded as a zero mode; no persistence barcode inferred from floating-point reduction; no linking form claimed when orientation/nondegeneracy hypotheses are absent; no global anomaly inferred from torsion data alone
notes: Priority C for current physics, but foundational for trustworthy global/topological discovery.
Build on snf, cochain, exact sequences and bundle topology rather than adding another matrix SNF implementation.
A first release may cover Z and finite filtrations only.
